thread:
hana.sales: Quick presales question — enterprise wants a 2-week Dedicated POC on Azure. Must present a single trusted IPv4 for their perimeter team (one /32), and theyre also asking if keys can be scoped per-environment. Need lead times and a short summary I can include in the SOW.
leo.eng: We can do per-project API keys that route to a Dedicated pool. Keys can be timeboxed (TTL) for POCs.
tara.network: For a single IPv4 we need to use Azure NAT Gateway attached to a Public IP (or Public IP Prefix) tied to the clusterthat yields a stable SNAT address. If they require absolutely no change, we must avoid cross-region failover and keep HA within the same AZ and single NAT path.
hana.sales: What about AzureLoad Balancer or App GW? Any better for a single IP?
tara.network: Azure Standard LB + outbound rules can work, but NAT Gateway with a static Public IP is cleaner for stable egress. Public IP Prefix (a block) lets us guarantee an exact /32. Note: Azure might still SNAT from multiple ephemeral ports but IP remains same.
ben.solutions: Short SOW bullet points to copy: "Provision Dedicated cluster (4x GPU), allocate static NAT Gateway public IP (single /32), generate timeboxed API key scoped to project, run smoke tests, grant console access for monitoring."
hana.sales: How long to provision if we request today?
leo.eng: Typical path: 1) SOW signed and billing cleared (same day) 2) Network reserves Public IP (1 business day) 3) Infra spins the Dedicated pool and attaches NAT (1 day) 4) Keys + smoke tests (same day) => total 2-3 business days.
tara.network: If they insist on zero public IP (private-only), choose Private Endpoint peering. That removes public egress but needs their network team to accept peering and route egress through their firewall. Lead time longer (3-7 days depending on their approvals).\hannah.sales: (typo) meant hana.sales: Any sample firewall rule we can send them?
tara.network: Yes — suggest both IP and hostname to be allowed because some corporate proxies validate SNI:
ALLOW: 203.0.113.47/32 (static NAT IP)
ALLOW HOST: dedicated.az1.redwood.example.com
And ask them to whitelist TCP:443 to that IP and hostname.
ben.solutions: Example curl to verify from their environment:
```
curl -v --resolve "dedicated.az1.redwood.example.com:443:203.0.113.47" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" \
  https://dedicated.az1.redwood.example.com/v1/chat -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```
leo.eng: Note on certs: TLS terminates at our edge for hosted. For Private Endpoint + mTLS option we can configure mutual TLS termination if they need client certs — that's additional setup and requires cert exchange.
tara.network: Also call out DNS TTL behavior. If they rely purely on hostname allowlist and their firewall checks DNS frequently, small DNS changes are fine. For strict single-IP allowlist, prefer the /32 route.
hana.sales: Pricing: can you give a short phrase for the sales email?
leo.eng: "POC pricing: pro-rated Dedicated rate + one-time setup fee. For small evals we usually apply a POC credit or 30% off first month on case-by-case; finance to confirm."
hana.sales: Perfect. I'll include both options (static NAT /32 + timebox keys, or private endpoint w/ zero public IP) and ask which they prefer.
infra-bot: Created infra ticket INF-4620: allocate public IP 203.0.113.47 and schedule cluster create. Assigned tara.network. ETA 48h.
hana.sales: Thanks team — sending to customer now. Will update thread with their selection and the signed SOW.
